title: Midnight Ocean — Renewal & Regional Burst Playbook Review
summary: Review of renewal timelines, proposed capacity uplift for EU region, discussion of private VPC pilot and latency vs cost tradeoffs; agreed next steps to run a short throughput benchmark and update pricing for dedicated reserved capacity.
topics: Renewal timing and length of contract
Capacity uplift and burst strategy for EU region
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-14
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen, Priya Patel, Liam O'Connor (Redwood) — Jordan Reyes, Samir Kline, Fiona Park (Midnight Ocean)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Midnight Ocean is planning to renew in Q3; they are targeting EU expansion and want to add a private VPC pilot for regulatory reasons. Discussed options for dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted with fallback; agreed to run a throughput/latency benchmark on a representative workload next week. Procurement needs an SOW and updated pricing table.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Maya from Redwood here, with Priya and Liam. Jordan?
[00:08] Jordan (Customer): Hey, yeah Jordan here. Sam's on as well. Fiona will be joining in a few.
[00:15] Priya (SE): Hi all. I know last time we sketched the EU burst, wanted to pick up where we left off — sizing and the VPC pilot ask.
[00:24] Jordan: Yep that's right. We've got regulatory checks in EU for a new product line so we need better residency and lower tail latency for EU users.
[00:33] Sam (SRE): Also want to validate failover behavior — if primary capacity hits the ceiling we need graceful fallback to the hosted model.
[00:40] Maya: Totally — that's one of the things Redwood's routing can do. Quick agenda: renewal term and start date, capacity sizing for EU, pilot for private VPC, security docs for procurement, and benchmark plan. Sound ok?
[00:51] Jordan: Yes. First up: renewal timeline. We're looking at a Sept 1 start ideally. Any constraints from your side?
[00:58] Liam (CSM): That's doable. We usually need a couple weeks to provision dedicated pools if reserved. If you want private onprem or VPC there's a bit more lead time — config and keys etc.
[01:10] Fiona (Procurement) [joins]: Sorry I'm late — Fiona from procurement. What pricing docs do you need?
[01:16] Maya: Hi Fiona — we'll send the updated pricing spreadsheet with a dedicated reserved capacity SKU and a VPC pilot line item. Also SOW and SOC 2 attestation.
[01:24] Fiona: Great, we need that for PO approval. Deadline for us is July 25 to start internal approvals.
[01:31] Priya: On the capacity side, Jordan shared last week the qps and token distribution; I put together two sizing options: a conservative uplift (30% spike headroom) and an aggressive burst plan using burst credits plus cold fallback. Which direction do you prefer?
[01:45] Jordan: We prefer aggressive for launch windows — worst-case latency matters more than incremental cost for the first quarter. But we also need a tight SLO for 95th percentile under 200ms for short responses.
[01:56] Sam: Is that 200ms total client-visible or token-to-token server? We need clarity.
[02:01] Jordan: Client-visible. End-to-end.
[02:04] Priya: Ok that affects batch sizing and routing — smaller batches, lower batching latency but higher unit cost. We can recommend a dedicated pool with smaller batch windows and prefix caching to reduce per-request tail.
[02:18] Sam: And for fallback — if the dedicated pool is saturated we want routed requests to the hosted model in the same region, correct? Not to a different region.
[02:25] Priya: Correct. We can route by region first, then by cost tier; fallback policy can be to same-region hosted instance. Slight chance of marginally higher latencies but avoids cross-region egress.
[02:36] Jordan: Can you quantify cost delta between dedicated small-batch config and hosted with caching?
[02:42] Maya: We'll surface exact numbers in the pricing sheet but ballpark — dedicated with small-batch optimized kernels is ~25–35% more per-token than a standard hosted config, but gains you deterministic tail latency and throughput. Hosted plus caching can be cheaper, but SLOs are less strict.
[03:00] Jordan: Understood. Security side: we need KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also proof of data residency for EU customer data.
[03:09] Liam: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS keys and audit export. We have an audit logs endpoint and can support SAML SSO and RBAC mapping. We'll attach the security whitepaper and your SOC 2 report.
[03:20] Fiona: Is there an additional charge for KMS/HSM integration?
[03:24] Maya: Not for the base VPC pilot — there is an enterprise add-on if you want an on-prem HSM certification, but typical KMS integration is included in the private plan.
[03:33] Sam: For the pilot, how much time do you need to stand up the VPC control plane? We're trying to plan a maintenance window.
[03:39] Priya: For a VPC pilot with reserved capacity and KMS — assuming certs and network peering are straightforward — expect 3 weeks from signed SOW. If there are unusual network approvals it can slip.
[03:51] Jordan: Timeline wise, if we want to start Sept 1, we need to sign by mid-August. Procurement needs the SOW by July 25 to make that feasible.
[04:00] Fiona: Yes, July 25 is firm on our side.
[04:03] Maya: We'll prioritize getting the SOW and pricing spreadsheet to you by July 20, that gives you five days for internal review.
[04:09] Jordan: Sounds good.
[04:13] Priya: About benchmarking — we propose a short throughput test next week: 2-hour run in EU region against the proposed model, including KV prefix caching turned on, and spike tests to 3x baseline. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and tail behavior. Any objections?
[04:28] Sam: No objections. Need to confirm an IP allowlist for the test nodes.
[04:32] Priya: We'll provide IPs. Also note transcriptions sometimes say KV cache as 'K V cash' — sorry about that — but we'll send the config.
[04:41] Jordan: Haha, ok. On model side — we're using a smaller Llama-ish open model variant. Are there kernel or quantization recommendations?
[04:49] Priya: Yes, we'll recommend int8 quant for the dedicated pool; runtime picks optimized kernels based on seq length distribution. Also we'll suggest KV cache hotwarm strategy to reduce repeated context cost.
[05:00] Jordan: Any impact to output quality?
[05:03] Priya: negligible for your workload (short completions), but we'll include evals from your prompt set in the benchmark.
[05:10] Maya: Quick note on commercial: if you commit to a 12-month reserved capacity for EU with a 20% uplift over current commit, we can offer a discounted step-down on per-token pricing and a waived setup fee for the VPC pilot.
[05:23] Fiona: That would be helpful. We need explicit numbers.
[05:27] Maya: We'll include two commitment tiers in the pricing doc.
[05:30] Jordan: Regarding fallback and graceful degradation — if the dedicated pool is overloaded, is the model variant the same or will it lower fidelity?
[05:38] Priya: Fallback can be configured either to the same model hosted variant or to a lower-cost quantized variant. We recommend same-model hosted for fidelity-sensitive paths and quantized for non-critical bulk calls.
[05:50] Sam: We have concerns about egress charges if fallback crosses region boundaries.
[05:54] Maya: We'll configure same-region fallback to avoid egress. If capacity is insufficient in-region the policy can expand to cross-region as last resort, with explicit tags so you can monitor egress costs.
[06:06] Jordan: Ok. Next, procurement checklist — Fiona what else do you need beyond SOW and pricing?
[06:12] Fiona: Standard PO, internal security checklist signoff, and an executed DPA. Can you attach the DPA and SOC 2 in the same email?
[06:18] Liam: Yes — we'll send SOC 2, DPA template, and the security whitepaper.
[06:22] Maya: I'll also attach an example SOW template, and include the timeline milestones.
[06:27] Jordan: Great. Any blockers on Redwood's side to meet July 20 SOW?
[06:31] Priya: No blockers, we just need the final qps numbers and sample payloads for the benchmark, which Jordan said he'd share.
[06:38] Jordan: I'll drop the payload and qps spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow.
[06:42] Maya: Perfect.
[06:45] -- (longer discussion about specific token distributions and cache warming — transcript abridged) --
[25:18] Priya: For the benchmark we'll also capture KV hit rates and cold-start penalties. Please note logging level — we can increase tracing but that affects latency slightly.
[25:30] Sam: Keep default tracing; we only need traces for failures.
[25:34] Priya: Got it.
[36:05] Jordan: On billing, if we do a commitment, what happens to unused reserved capacity? Can credits roll over?
[36:12] Maya: We typically have a monthly unsettled reserve model — unused committed units can be used for burst within the term but don't roll beyond the contract. We can discuss a more flexible rollover for enterprise agreements.
[36:25] Fiona: We should see that in the commercial annex.
[36:28] Maya: We'll include a proposed annex with rollover options.
[36:32] Jordan: Any competitors in your field we should be aware of? (laughs)
[36:36] Maya: Customers sometimes compare us to Anthropic-hosted and to self-hosted solutions on CloudX. We'll surface differentiation points in the materials.
[36:45] Jordan: Ok.
[45:02] Liam: Wrapping up — agreed next steps: Redwood to send SOW/pricing/security pack by July 20; Midnight Ocean to provide qps and sample payloads by July 15; schedule the 2-hour EU benchmark next week (TBD) with IP allowlist; procurement to begin internal approval by July 25.
[45:20] Fiona: Confirmed.
[45:23] Jordan: One more thing — can Priya share a short runbook for failover behavior so our oncall knows what to expect?
[45:29] Priya: Yes — I'll draft a 1-pager and include it with the benchmark results.
[45:33] Maya: Excellent. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with artifacts.
[45:39] -- Call ends --
